card.name: Gnawa
card.era: Sub-Saharan African heritage in Morocco · UNESCO 2019
card.tagline: Morocco's UNESCO-listed trance dance — Sufi brotherhoods of West African descent, iron krakebs castanets driving all-night lila ceremonies.
card.profile: Gnawa music is a body of Moroccan religious songs and rhythms. Emerging in the 16th and 17th centuries, Gnawa music developed through the cultural fusion of West Africans brought to Morocco, notably the Hausa, Fulani, and Bambara peoples, whose presence and heritage are reflected in the songs and rituals.
card.insight: On December 12, 2019, Gnawa was officially inscribed at UNESCO's 14th session held in Bogotá, Colombia.
